author: agent
log: Rule: every part is named from its own island's evidence only: <shape>_<sizeX>x<sizeY>x<sizeZ>. Shape category from sorted size ratios: Flat_Sheet if thinnest dimension < 0.02; Long_Bar if longest/shortest >= 6 and middle/shortest < 2; Plate if middle/shortest >= 2.5; otherwise Block. Dimensions are the report's size in x,y,z order, rounded to 0.1 ('p' for the decimal point).

Where two or more islands of ONE mesh share the same shape name, position tokens from `at` are appended: x<0.34 Left, >0.66 Right else Centre; y<0.34 Low, >0.66 High else Mid; z<0.34 Front, >0.66 Back else Middle. Assumes +x is right and +y is up; which z end is the front is a guess, so Front/Back only means low-z/high-z.

Where identical names remained across different meshes (the evidence for those meshes is identical: same material, triangle count, size), a _CopyA/_CopyB suffix was added in mesh order. The suffix carries no evidence; it only keeps names unique. Many meshes appear in identical pairs or as a multi-island mesh plus a single-island twin with the same island size and triangle count.

No function was named anywhere: the evidence has no colours, no textures, no uv, only material names, sizes, triangle counts and `at`. Material names (Material_20 to Material_29) are opaque, so they were used only as the unit of cutting (mesh = one material) and not in names or `basis`. All names are therefore shape-descriptive abstentions. Part names contain digits (the dimensions) but are not numbered placeholders.

Every island is its own part (identical things in one mesh are separate parts per the brief), including 1 to 7 triangle zero-thickness facets in meshes 54/58; I kept them separate rather than merging, which makes those meshes noisy (22 parts each).

The brief says the report includes colours with shares; this evidence file has none (every island says 'no texture', no uv). I noted this and did not invent colour evidence. `basis` therefore uses only size, shape and (where island positions disambiguate) position.

Single-island meshes always report at 0.5,0.5,0.5, so no position evidence exists for them: each is `whole`. Position of a mesh in the scene is unknown, which also means mirrored twins (e.g. meshes 46 vs 65 vs 71) cannot be told apart by anything but within-mesh `at`.

The check command and SEG plan syntax needed no special handling; group names are '<first part name>_Cluster' for multi-island meshes and '<part name>_Unit' for whole-mesh parts, which carry no extra information.
